summary.intent: Make parseBody() and validator() match Content-Type media types case-insensitively (issue #5060) while leaving parameters such as multipart boundaries intact.
summary.issue_fit: Partial — mixed-case media types now parse in parseBody(), validator('json') and validator('form'), but the parseBody() rewrite regresses reading a body after c.req.formData() (see finding).

findings.title: Reuse cached FormData in parseFormData
findings.trigger: A handler calls await c.req.formData() and then await c.req.parseBody() on the same request; parseFormData now reads request.arrayBuffer(), which HonoRequest rebuilds from the cached FormData with a fresh boundary, and parses it with the original Content-Type.
findings.impact: Multipart requests fail with 'Failed to parse body as FormData' (HTTP 500) and urlencoded requests silently return one garbage key instead of the submitted fields; the merge-base returned the correct fields for both.
findings.change: In parseFormData, when the request is a HonoRequest and bodyCache.formData is already set, await that cached FormData and convert it directly; otherwise keep the arrayBuffer path with bufferToFormData. Add a regression test for formData() followed by parseBody().
findings.source: Issue #5060, expected behavior: only media-type case matching was to change.

observations.fact: The method-override middleware still matches Content-Type with case-sensitive startsWith checks, so mixed-case media types are treated differently there than in parseBody().
At head, c.req.text() followed by c.req.parseBody() on a form body now succeeds, where the merge-base threw a Content-Type error.
observations.evidence: Scratch probe text-then-parse at head (200) versus base (500).
